_comment: Job templates ('productions'). tier = minimum tier. statWeights sum to 1. flavour = 3 'script' variants.

flavour: INT. LATE-NIGHT GROCERY. A bored clerk, a jar of pickled eggs and a till that hasn't been emptied since Tuesday.
A low-budget opener. One loud entrance, one quiet exit, and nobody touches the lottery tickets.
The owner keeps his takings under the cigarette rack. Everybody in the neighbourhood knows. Now so do you.
A cherry-red coupe parked outside the country club. The valet is on a smoke break for exactly four minutes.
EXT. CAR DEALERSHIP - NIGHT. Rows of chrome under sodium lights. Pick the one with the fewest dents and the loudest stereo.
A collector wants a convertible with fins. He doesn't want to know where it came from. Neither do the insurers.
An insurance firm keeps its client ledger on a mainframe the size of a wardrobe. Bring a very long cable.
The phone company's switchboard room. Tap the line, record the tones, sell the numbers. Very modern.
A rival studio's accounts are on magnetic tape in the basement. Copy the reel, swap the labels, walk out humming.
Sixty seconds. One display case, one brick, one engine already running. Action!
The jeweller on Fifth just got a shipment of sapphires and a brand-new window. Only one of those survives the night.
A ring-heavy window display, a Sunday-night crowd and a getaway car double-parked with its hazards on.
A gala opening. Canapes, champagne and a small oil painting nobody will miss until the critics arrive.
The Face charms the curator about brushwork. The Ghost leaves through the skylight with the brushwork.
A modern art exhibit. Half the guests won't notice the frame is empty. The other half will call it a statement.
A high-roller with a borrowed accent, a rigged roulette wheel and a pit boss who loves a good story.
The casino's new electronic slot machines talk to a computer in the back. Teach it some new manners.
Comp the suite, charm the cashier, swap the chips. The house always wins. Tonight, you're the house.
The Friday payroll run takes the tunnel at 6:15. A stalled ice-cream van, a crowbar and a very polite request.
A car-chase set piece: box the truck in on the overpass, crack the back doors before the sirens get a close-up.
The guards stop for doughnuts at the same diner every shift. Their truck does not stop being full of money.
First National's vault door weighs eleven tons and hasn't met you yet. Long weekend. Long take.
Tunnel in from the dry cleaner's next door. Mind the steam pipes and do not, under any circumstances, take the shirts.
The alarm company is running a 'routine test' tonight. You know this because you booked it.
The Grand Palace Theatre, opening night. Red carpet, searchlights, and the box-office vault holding a month of takings. Roll camera.
Every star in town will be in the stalls. Every guard will be watching the stars. The vault is backstage, behind the orchestra pit.
Your magnum opus. Five specialists, one night, one take. When the house lights come up, the safe should be empty and you should be gone.
